Figure 56. Hour VMT fractions for FleetDNA single-unit short-haul vehicles FleetDNA data on refuse trucks show higher proportions of miles driven during the morning (Figure 57). It is interesting that FleetDNA also shows somewhat bimodal distributions, but the two modes are much closer together in the morning than the spread of MOVES3 peaks. Urban other roads on weekdays have around 20 vehicles and hundreds of hours per hour ID on average, and will constitute an adjustment to MOVES3 after the data have been further fortified by CE- CERT data. Urban other roads on weekends tracked less data and would need further studies to amend. The urban freeways hourly distribution is noisy and only based on seven vehicles and 3 hours per vehicle (refer to Section 4.1); this group will be improved by additional CE-CERT data in several subsections. 76 This report is available at no cost from the National Laboratory of the Rockies (NLR) at www.nlr.gov/publications. Figure 57. Hour VMT fractions for FleetDNA refuse trucks For transit buses, the FleetDNA data match very closely to MOVES3 VMT distributions for urban other roads (Figure 58). It appears that transit bus activity follows the pattern of personal vehicle traffic, which dominates the trend in the MOVES3 default VMT distributions. The FleetDNA data on urban freeways on weekdays are more sparse, with buses spending much less time on most hour IDs than for the bottom row (refer to Section 4.1). Because the FleetDNA transit sample—at 16 buses—was smaller than other source types and the distributions from the transit bus are noisier but have similar trends as the MOVES3 defaults, we would recommend keeping the default MOVES3 distributions for this source type if based solely on FleetDNA. We will revisit recommendations in the combined data section. 77 This report is available at no cost from the National Laboratory of the Rockies (NLR) at www.nlr.gov/publications. Figure 58. Hour VMT fractions for FleetDNA transit buses For urban other roads on weekdays, FleetDNA school buses showed a bimodal trend, with peaks approximately aligning with the hour ID of MOVES3 peaks. Also, as expected, the FleetDNA data do not show activity extending into the evening hours, as shown for the default MOVES3 VMT distribution. The FleetDNA data sample was very small for this source type (four buses), but we believe it is more representative than the current MOVES3 default for national school buses. The FleetDNA VMT distribution data may be useful to combine with future data on other school buses to develop a more representative characterization of school bus VMT distributions. Figure 59.
